text:
samir: hi all — starting today! i'm on Ubuntu 22.04 inside WSL2. following the onboarding but hitting a few weird things: asdf python install fails with a compile error, pip wants openssl headers, and my dotfiles' shell init doesn't seem to load asdf into non-login shells. also 1password op signin works locally but the devcontainer doesn't see OP_SESSION. who to bug for quick tips?

noelle: welcome Samir! for Ubuntu you usually need the build deps: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev libffi-dev pkg-config` — that fixes most python compile errors for asdf.

rachel: couple of dotfile gotchas: make sure `~/.asdf` is on your PATH and that your shell startup runs `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` (bash) or `eval "$(asdf init -)"` in fish/zsh. WSL sometimes spawns non-login shells for terminals, so add the init to both `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc` (or your distro's shell rc) so GUI terminals pick it up. After that run `asdf reshim` and restart the shell.

samir: i had `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` but forgot the `eval "$(asdf init)"` bit. fixed that and `asdf list` now shows installed versions. still, when i `pip wheel -w build .` in a project i get `openssl/ssl.h: No such file or directory`.

noelle: `libssl-dev` is the missing piece. also check `python-config --cflags` or `pkg-config --cflags openssl` to validate. If you installed openssl from source earlier, set `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/opt/openssl/lib` or adjust `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`.

samir: installed libssl-dev and now the wheel compiles, thanks. quick Q: our onboarding dotfiles repo has a `bootstrap.sh` that calls `direnv allow`, but inside a devcontainer direnv is prompting and the container build fails. any pattern to pre-authorize?

rachel: avoid auto-approving direnv in builds — better pattern is to add a short `postCreateCommand` in `devcontainer.json` which runs `op signin --raw > /tmp/op_token && export OP_SESSION_my=$(cat /tmp/op_token)` and then `direnv allow` as an explicit step, or mount a `.envrc.local` from the host with limited secrets. Also ensure `direnv hook bash` is in your `~/.bashrc` so non-interactive shells don't error out.

devex-bot: Developer setup checklist: https://intranet.redwood/dev-setup/linux - has WSL tips, asdf init examples, and devcontainer patterns.

samir: thanks — one more: ssh agent forwarding. i `ssh -A jumpbox` but when i `ssh-add -l` on the jumpbox it shows no identities. locally `ssh-add -l` shows my key.

noelle: for WSL make sure your Windows ssh-agent isn't interfering. either run `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` in WSL and `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, or enable Windows OpenSSH agent and forward it. Check `ssh -v -A jumpbox` to see if agent forwarding is negotiated. If the jumpbox's sshd disables forwarding, infra will need to flip `AllowAgentForwarding`.

infra-bot: Hi Samir — if the jumpbox needs a config change we can request it. Opened REQ-2041 referencing your username; infra will follow up in a DM.

samir: great, i'll DM infra-bot. final tiny annoyance: my `~/.gitconfig` from dotfiles references `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` but inside the devcontainer the path is missing. any safe way to share keys without copying private keys into containers?

rachel: recommended: use `ssh-agent` forwarding into the container instead of copying keys. You can enable `remoteEnv` in `devcontainer.json` and start the container with a bind mount to the ssh agent socket (`-v $SSH_AUTH_SOCK:/ssh-agent -e SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent`) in your devcontainer launch config. That keeps keys on the host.

samir: this is super helpful — fixed asdf init, installed libssl-dev, and will follow up on the jumpbox. thank you all! i'll update the onboarding doc if i hit doc gaps. :smile:
